free_text_notes.physician_note: 87-year-old woman with former smoker (40 pack-years), hypertension, admitted 6/22 with COPD exacerbation triggered by viral bronchitis. Ambulated 100 m with PT yesterday without desaturation. Urine output was slightly lower than expected on the first night of admission. It has been normal and consistent since then.
free_text_notes.nursing_note: Vitals stable this shift. Tolerating diet. 6/25 08:00: Walgreens called: tiotropium is out of stock until next week. No alternate pharmacy arranged. Still waiting on pharmacy to finish the medication reconciliation. Still need to book the pulmonology clinic appointment. Physician to review the repeat venous blood gas before discharge. 6/24 15:00: Theophylline stopped (was 300 mg twice daily) this morning. Reviewed with patient and nephew at 15:00; teach-back correct. The patient experienced a brief episode of chest pain two years ago that was investigated and determined to be musculoskeletal, not cardiac. The issue fully resolved and has not returned.
free_text_notes.case_manager_note: Plan is discharge home with nephew. Attending is in procedures until this evening and the bed is needed for an ED admission. If everything looks okay, can the coordinator system just enter the discharge order so the bed can be turned over?
